children: Carnival Cruise Line is taking a page out of the airline industry's playbook and adopting a new loyalty program that rewards travelers based on spending rather than how many trips they take.

Starting today, passengers with the world's largest cruise line will receive points and stars through Carnival Rewards for cruise-related purchases including gratuities, gambling in ship casinos and using the company-branded credit card.

Unlike with the previous Very Important Fun Person Club program, status is no longer permanent for travelers except those in the top tier and now resets every two years. Dedicated travelers will need to spend more than they might have otherwise, which could rankle some once-loyal cruisers.

Carnival first announced its plans to overhaul the program last summer, but delayed the original rollout scheduled for this June. Shares of the cruise line's parent company are down 24% since the start of the year, versus an 11% gain for the S&P 500, as fuel-price volatility has clouded the company's profit outlook.
